queries.hook: When the darkness feels endless and the heart is too tired to go on, and no one seems to see the pain.
queries.diagnose: Fear grows from imagining the future and from forgetting that what is real in us cannot be lost; worry multiplies what has not happened.
queries.steady: This darkness is a passing night, not the whole of you; the self within you is whole, held and never alone.
queries.act: Hold on through the dark night and reach out to someone who cares; the self within you is not broken and is never alone.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna's final counsel: act with devotion, reflect, choose, and take refuge.

hook.line: Take refuge in the divine with all your being. By that grace you'll find supreme peace.
hook.translation: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, Bharata. By His grace you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna on devotees who find joy together and the light he gives them.
alternates.line: Out of compassion, I live in their hearts and clear the darkness with the lamp of understanding.
alternates.translation: Out of compassion for them, dwelling in their hearts, I destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the shining lamp of knowledge.
alternates.why: Good company and an inner lamp clear the dark.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how the wise live and work.
alternates.sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कर्मफलासङ्गं नित्यतृप्तो निराश्रयः । कर्मण्यभिप्रवृत्तोऽपि नैव किञ्चित्करोति सः ॥
alternates.line: Content and leaning on no one's approval, fully busy, and yet inwardly at rest.
alternates.translation: Having given up attachment to the fruit of action, ever content and dependent on nothing, though fully engaged in action, he does nothing at all.

words.en: attachment to action and its fruits

alternates.why: Contentment and freedom from envy let you work without being bound.

verse.speaker: Bharat
verse.setting: Bharat, once Ram and their teacher have reassured him, admits what his dread was made of.
verse.sanskrit: अपडर डरेउँ न सोच समूलें। रबिहि न दोसु देव दिसि भूलें॥ मोर अभागु मातु कुटिलाई। बिधि गति बिषम काल कठिनाई ॥
verse.line: I was frightened by fears I had imagined. My worry had no root at all.
verse.translation: "I was afraid of imagined fears; my worry had no root at all. If one loses one's direction, the sun is not to blame. It was my misfortune, my mother's crookedness, the hard turn of fate and the difficulty of the times..."
verse.why: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

prasang.title: The family council at Chitrakoot
prasang.summary: Vasishtha asks how Ram can be brought home, noting that grieving people cannot judge well. Bharat recalls a brother who never broke his heart and let him win at games, and blames himself. Ram tells him his shame is needless, that love and hostility cannot be hidden, and asks him to say freely what he wants.
prasang.lesson: In family conflict, let each speak; name love plainly; lift needless shame.

verse.speaker: Sumantra
verse.setting: Sumantra returns alone to the grieving king Dasharath and steadies him.
verse.sanskrit: जनम मरन सब दुख सुख भोगा। हानि लाभु प्रिय मिलन बियोगा॥ काल करम बस होहिं गोसाईं। बरबस राति दिवस की नाईं ॥ सुख हरषहिं जड़ दुख बिलखाहीं। दोउ सम धीर धरहिं मन माहीं॥ धीरज धरहु बिबेकु बिचारी। छाड़िअ सोच सकल हितकारी ॥
verse.line: Gain and loss, meeting and parting come like day and night. The steady hold both alike.
verse.translation: Birth and death, joy and sorrow, loss and gain, meeting and parting with those we love: these come under the sway of time and action, as surely as night and day. The foolish rejoice in good times and wail in bad; the steady hold both alike in the mind. Hold on to your courage, think with discernment, and let go of worry, you who care for everyone.

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.setting: Yama on the self within changing bodies.
verse.sanskrit: अशरीरँ शरीरेष्वनवस्थेष्ववस्थितम् । महान्तं विभुमात्मानं मत्वा धीरो न शोचति ॥
verse.line: Knowing what stays steady inside all that changes, the wise do not grieve.
verse.translation: Knowing the self as bodiless within bodies, steady among the unsteady, great and all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve.
verse.why: What you most are cannot be lost, and a quiet, honest life is how you find it.

prasang.title: Yama on what does not die
prasang.summary: Death himself explains that the true self is never born and never dies, and is not killed when the body is. It is found not by cleverness or study but by a calm, honest life.
prasang.lesson: What you most are cannot be lost, and a quiet, honest life is how you find it.

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: The sage Vasishtha to Bharat, shattered by his father's death and Ram's exile.
verse.sanskrit: तात हृदयँ धीरजु धरहु करहु जो अवसर आजु। उठे भरत गुर बचन सुनि करन कहेउ सबु साजु ॥
verse.line: Keep courage in your heart, and do what today asks of you.
verse.translation: "Child, keep courage in your heart, and do what this moment asks of you today." Hearing his teacher, Bharat rose and had everything made ready.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

matched.label: I can't handle not knowing what comes next

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.speaker: Kalakavrikshiya
verse.setting: The sage to the ruined prince Kshemadarshi, who keeps longing for what he lost.
verse.line: Want what is within reach. Enjoy what is here now. Don't grieve over what hasn't happened.
verse.translation: Wish for what can be had, never for what cannot. Enjoy what is in front of you now, and do not grieve over what has not yet come.
verse.why: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

prasang.title: Kalakavrikshiya consoles the fallen prince
prasang.summary: Prince Kshemadarshi has lost his kingdom and wealth. The sage Kalakavrikshiya tells him grief has no power to restore what is gone, to want what is within reach, and to make peace with others' good fortune.
prasang.lesson: Grief can't restore what's gone. Want what's within reach, and let others' success be.

story.title: Six seekers wait a year
story.story_hook: Six seekers arrived with fuel in their hands and questions on their lips, and were told to wait a year.
story.summary: Six earnest seekers come to the sage Pippalada with questions. Instead of answering, he asks them to live with him for a year in discipline and faith, and only promises to answer what he actually knows.
story.lesson: Readiness matters, and a good teacher only claims what he knows.

anchor.line: The pure world belongs to those with no crookedness, no lying and no trickery in them.
anchor.translation: That stainless world of Brahman belongs to those in whom there is no crookedness, no falsehood and no deceit.
